title: Adoptive Transfer of CX3CR1-Transduced Tregs Homing to the Forebrain in LPS-Induced Neuroinflammation and 3xTg Alzheimer's Disease Models
content: CX3CR1-transduced regulatory T cells (Tregs) have shown potential in reducing neuroinflammation by targeting microglial activation. Reactive microglia are implicated in neurological disorders, and CX3CR1-CX3CL1 signaling modulates microglial activity. The ability of CX3CR1-transduced Tregs to inhibit LPS-induced neuroinflammation was assessed in animal models. CX3CR1 Tregs were administered to LPS-induced and 3xTG Alzheimer’s mouse models, resulting in reduced proinflammatory marker expression in both the cortices and hippocampi. In the 3xTG Alzheimer’s model, neuroinflammation was significantly reduced, demonstrating the efficacy of CX3CR1 Tregs even in chronic neuroinflammatory conditions. These findings highlight the therapeutic potential of CX3CR1 Treg therapy in modulating microglial activity and offer promising treatment strategies for neurodegenerative diseases.
